entry.title: Maintenance Order Job Card – Email not triggered after changing recipient with Immediate dispatch
entry.content: S/4HANA 2023 FPS03 – Maintenance Order JOB_CARD email output. Dispatch Time is configured as Immediate. The customer does not accept the additional save as a solution because Immediate dispatch is required.  immediate output processing under PM-WOC-MO-PRI and provide the applicable standard correction/SAP Note for the installed S/4HANA 2023 FPS03 level.

entry.title: What triggers the next call in a maintenance plan?
entry.content:
Hi there. I'm a maint supervisor wanting to understand maint plan logic a bit better.

I work with equipment that have time based maintenance plans setup for 12 month inspections, the notifications will auto generate 90 days before the work is required. They also have a "serviceable" "not serviceable" measurement point.

After the physical inspection work is done, there are 4 places where dates are input in sap:

1. In the notification 'dates' tab:

a. "Completion date", and

b.  "Date of inspection"

2. In the measurement document:

a. "Date of measurement point" 

b. "Expiry date"

I am just wondering which one of these dates does SAP use to generate the date that the next notification is generated?

entry.title: Best Practice for non-executed routine 1 monthly maintenance Work Orders
entry.content:
Dear all,

Closely consider this situation,
Let's say, we have 1 monthly routine preventive maintenance work orders on some low-risk (not SCE) equipment in the asset. However, due to some issues, the work could not be performed for four consecutive months. This status quo will remain till the 8th month.
We are already in the fifth month and the Work Order has already called on SAP for the 5th and 6th months.
What is the best practise for the Work Orders that were not executed in the field?

 - Request for deviation/deferral of their LAFDs?
- or close and TECO the Work Orders at Zero manhours?

- or Cancel (CNCL) / AWAC the Work Orders?

Furthermore, should the 5th and 6th month's Work Orders be planned, or left on INIT status?
Note that if we defer the earlier four work orders to the 8th Month, this would imply having to deal with eight 1-monthly Work Orders for same activity, same equipment in the eight month.

entry.title: SAP EAM Planned Jobs_Future team Visibility for planned jobs
entry.content:
Future team Visibility for planned jobs-

The requirement of user stories is that—as a planner, I want to see the assigned team for planned jobs, so that I can forecast future workload and resource application

Current Gap – team is visible only after an order created in IP19 and IP24, do not provide the required operation team forecast.

A solution is needed for future workload forecasting to allow visibility of the team who will be carrying out the work on planned jobs.

Current Scenario in our S/4 system—There is a custom lookup table that holds the mapping of the work center against the location and standard STK code (which is the job type). But these STK codes are derived from the task list operation when job created from the maintenance plan. But our requirement is to forecast the responsible team against the asset before the job is created. Unless the job/operation-created system does not know what type of job code (STK codes) and which team is responsible.

The requirement is to find out who is responsible for the asset against the location.

Do we have any solution options?

Note - We derived Locaton from the equipment master. And the main work center is an asset, which is mostly a default work center; that is the reason it does not show which teams are responsible, like when an order is created that has an actual work center against the operation line. Is there a way we can update the responsible team at the asset level based on location? We have GIS integration to get the responsible work center based on location. Can we use equipment classification or partner data to update the responsible team? So that we can build a report around assets, saying which team are responsible for these assets in that particular location?

Thanks in advance.

Regards,

Amitabh

entry.title: Record Time Option Is Not Displayed in the Perform Maintenance Jobs App
entry.content:
Hi Experts

Start and Record Time buttons are not visible in the system.

I enabled Confirm Jobs Without Assignment in the app configuration. However, the Start and Record Time buttons are still unavailable.

I also noticed a difference from Private Cloud: the Perform Jobs and Record Time Without Personnel Number setting is available there, but I cannot find it in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608.

1. Could you please confirm whether this setting is supported in Public Cloud and advise what is required to enable these buttons?

2. In a phase based maintenance process, are operations required to be dispatched before they appear in the Perform Maintenance Jobs? In my test, the operation appeared only after dispatching. However, I remember that in Private Cloud, the operations appeared in this app even before they weren't dispatched.

The documentation in the link included information about this;

https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_ON-PREMISE/e72f747389b340229f7fa343975bfa57/3da57072a73444f18b5ad8785bc2900e.html

*A job is a maintenance order operation or suboperation that is ready for execution. This means that the relevant operations or suboperations are in the Ready for Execution, Work in Execution, Work Paused, or Work Finished subphase. The list also includes jobs that do not support the phase model. In this case, the corresponding orders must be released. For such jobs, subphase details are not available.*

Thank you!

entry.title: Planning Buckets Background Job Timing Not Aligned
entry.content:
We are experiencing an issue with Planning Buckets where the bucket configuration timing and the background job execution timing are not aligned.

For example, the planning bucket is configured with a start time of 12:00 AM (UTC), whereas the corresponding background job is executed at 03:00 AM (UTC+3). Due to this timing difference, some maintenance work orders that should not belong to a particular weekly bucket are being included in that bucket's work list.

Our initial assessment suggests that recreating the background jobs and scheduling them with revised timings could potentially resolve the issue. However, this is not a preferred solution, as there are multiple background jobs already configured in the system, and recreating them would require significant administrative effort.

We are seeking guidance on the most efficient way to resolve this timing misalignment between Planning Buckets and background jobs. Recreating all existing jobs would involve considerable effort due to the number of jobs currently configured. We would appreciate any recommendations, best practices, or alternative approaches to address this issue while ensuring correct work order assignment to planning buckets.

Thank you in advance for your support and guidance.
